claim: TRPV1 channels are gated by a variety of thermal, chemical, and mechanical stimuli.
source: TRPV1 channels are gated by a variety of thermal, chemical, and mechanical stimuli.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature establishing these gating mechanisms.

claim: The opening of single TRPV1 channels produced sparklets, representing localized regions of elevated Ca2+.
source: The opening of single TRPV1 channels produced sparklets, representing localized regions of elevated Ca2+.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental observations shown in figures and videos.

claim: Unlike sparklets reported for L-type Ca2+ channels, TRPV4 channels, and AchR channels, TRPV1 channels diffused laterally in the plasma membrane as they gated.
source: Unlike sparklets reported for L-type Ca2+ channels, TRPV4 channels, and AchR channels, TRPV1 channels diffused laterally in the plasma membrane as they gated.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data and comparison to cited literature on other channel types.

claim: Mobility of TRPV1 was highly variable from channel-to-channel and, to a smaller extent, from cell to cell.
source: Mobility was highly variable from channel-to-channel and, to a smaller extent, from cell to cell.
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 4 and related data.

claim: Mobility of TRPV1 decreased upon channel activation by capsaicin, but only in the presence of extracellular Ca2+.
source: Most surprisingly, we found that mobility decreased upon channel activation by capsaicin, but only in the presence of extracellular Ca2+.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Decreased mobility of open TRPV1 could act as a diffusion trap to concentrate channels in cell regions with high activity.
source: We propose that decreased mobility of open TRPV1 could act as a diffusion trap to concentrate channels in cell regions with high activity.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: TRPV1 gating is regulated by extracellular protons, phosphorylation by PKC, phosphorylation by PKA, temperature, fatty acids such as lysophosphatidic acid and anandamide, phosphoinositide signaling lipids, eicosanoids, and capsaicin.
source: Its gating is multimodal, regulated by extracellular protons, phosphorylation by PKC, phosphorylation by PKA, temperature, fatty acids such as lysophosphatidic acid and anandamide, phosphoinositide signaling lipids, eicosanoids, and capsaicin, the pungent extract of hot chili peppers (Caterina et al., 1997; Zygmunt et al., 1999; Premkumar and Ahern, 2000; Bhave et al., 2002; Hu et al., 2002; Pomonis et al., 2003; Klein et al., 2008; Ufret-Vincenty et al., 2011; Nieto-Posadas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: TRPV1 is subject to indirect regulation by G-protein coupled receptors and intracellular Ca2+.
source: Furthermore, it is also subject to indirect regulation by G-protein coupled receptors and intracellular Ca2+ and its trafficking can be regulated by receptor tyrosine kinases (Chuang et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2005, 2008; Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: TRPV1 trafficking can be regulated by receptor tyrosine kinases.
source: Furthermore, it is also subject to indirect regulation by G-protein coupled receptors and intracellular Ca2+ and its trafficking can be regulated by receptor tyrosine kinases (Chuang et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2005, 2008; Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: TRPV1 channels are highly permeable to Ca2+, with PNa:PCa estimated to be at least 1:10.
source: TRPV1 channels are highly permeable to Ca2+, with PNa:PCa estimated to be at least 1:10 (Caterina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ca2+ imaging at the whole-cell level was used in the seminal tour-de-force that first identified TRPV1 as the capsaicin-activated ion channel.
source: Indeed, Ca2+ imaging at the whole-cell level was used in the seminal tour-de-force that first identified TRPV1 as the capsaicin-activated ion channel (Caterina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The high permeability of TRPV1 to Ca2+ has been a useful tool in high-throughput screening of regulatory compounds.
source: The high permeability of TRPV1 to Ca2+ has also been a useful tool in high-throughput screening of regulatory compounds and led to the identification of a family of toxins, first purified from spiders, that act as potent activators of TRPV1 (and have enhanced the survival of the spiders) (Caterina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A family of toxins, first purified from spiders, act as potent activators of TRPV1.
source: The high permeability of TRPV1 to Ca2+ has also been a useful tool in high-throughput screening of regulatory compounds and led to the identification of a family of toxins, first purified from spiders, that act as potent activators of TRPV1 (and have enhanced the survival of the spiders) (Caterina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ca2+ influx through TRPV1 desensitizes sensory neurons.
source: In addition, Ca2+ influx through TRPV1 desensitizes sensory neurons (Cholewinski et al., 1993; Koplas et al., 1997; Rosenbaum et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of the signaling lipid phosphoinositide 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) via Ca2+-mediated activation of phospholipase C appears to contribute to desensitization of TRPV1 during periods of high channel activity.
source: Although multiple pathways are likely involved in neuronal desensitization, depletion of the signaling lipid phosphoinositide 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) via Ca2+-mediated activation of phospholipase C appears to contribute to desensitization of TRPV1 during periods of high channel activity (Stein et al., 2006; Lukacs et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: When Ca2+-permeable channels open, localized Ca2+ influx produces a fluorescent 'sparklet' in the cytosol proximal to the active channel.
source: When Ca2+-permeable channels open, localized Ca2+ influx produces a fluorescent 'sparklet' in the cytosol proximal to the active channel (Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The presence of nonfluorescent Ca2+ chelator in the cell acts as a sink for the excess Ca2+, enhancing the localization of the source of the influx.
source: The presence of the nonfluorescent Ca2+ chelator in the cell acts as a sink for the excess Ca2+, enhancing the localization of the source of the influx (Navedo et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Optical approaches have been used to record the activity of L-type Ca2+ channels in urinary bladder smooth muscle, arterial smooth muscle, ventricular myocytes, and mammalian cell lines.
source: Optical approaches have been used to record the activity of L-type Ca2+ channels in urinary bladder smooth muscle (Sidaway and Teramoto, 2014), arterial smooth muscle (Navedo et al., 2006; Amberg et al., 2007; Navedo et al., 2010; Tajada et al., 2013), ventricular myocytes (Wang et al., 2001; Zhou et al., 2009), and mammalian cell lines (Gulia et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Sparklets due to TRPV4 channels have been reported in arterial smooth muscle and vascular endothelium.
source: More recently, sparklets due to TRPV4 channels have been reported in arterial smooth muscle (Mercado et al., 2014) and vascular endothelium (Bagher et al., 2012; Sonkusare et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Multiple channels were typically clustered at the sparklet sites from L-type Ca2+ channels and TRPV4 channels.
source: First, multiple channels were typically clustered at the sparklet sites.
evidence: This is based on prior reports about L-type Ca2+ channels and TRPV4 channels.

claim: Sparklets from L-type Ca2+ channels and TRPV4 channels remained stationary throughout the observation period.
source: Second, the sparklets remained stationary throughout the observation period.
evidence: This is based on prior reports about L-type Ca2+ channels and TRPV4 channels.

claim: The fluorescence signals emanating from muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChR) expressed in Xenopus oocytes did not indicate channel clustering at the fluorescence sites.
source: It should be noted that the muscle nicotinic aceytylcholine receptors (AChR) expressed in Xenopus oocytes have also been studied by optical recording, and the fluorescence signals emanating from these channels did not indicate channel clustering at the fluorescence sites (Demuro and Parker, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: All fluorescence Ca2+ signals from AChR maintained a constant position for the duration of the optical recordings.
source: Nevertheless, the authors did find that all fluorescence Ca2+ signals from AChR maintained a constant position for the duration of the optical recordings.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Regulation of mobility in the plasma membrane has been identified as a key element in signaling for the Orai family of Ca2+-release activated channels (CRAC).
source: Regulation of mobility in the plasma membrane has been identified as a key element in signaling for the Orai family of Ca2+-release activated channels (CRAC).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on Orai channels.

claim: Orai channels diffuse throughout the plasma membrane in resting cells, but in response to the emptying of Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) they cluster at sites in the surface membrane that juxtapose to the ER.
source: Orai channels diffuse throughout the plasma membrane in resting cells, but in response to the emptying of Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) they cluster at sites in the surface membrane that juxtapose to the ER (Lioudyno et al., 2008; Penna et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The interaction of Orai channels with the ER-resident protein STIM1 reduces Orai mobility, acting as a sort of diffusion trap to localize Orai channels to these sites as well as directly gating Ca2+ influx through the Orai pore.
source: The interaction of Orai channels with the ER-resident protein STIM1 reduces Orai mobility, acting as a sort of diffusion trap to localize Orai channels to these sites as well as directly gating Ca2+ influx through the Orai pore (Yeromin et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Very little fluorescence was observed upon dialysis of Fluo-4/EGTA solution into the isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons via the patch pipette.
source: Very little fluorescence was observed upon dialysis of Fluo-4/ EGTA solution into the isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons via the patch pipette.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: Perfusion of 100 nM capsaicin into the bath generated localized bursts of fluorescence, termed sparklets.
source: However, subsequent perfusion of 100 nM capsaicin into the bath generated localized bursts of fluorescence, termed sparklets (Figure 1A and Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: Sparklets were observed with physiological concentrations of extracellular Ca2+ (2 mM).
source: Sparklets were observed with physiological concentrations of extracellular Ca2+ (2 mM).
evidence: This is an experimental condition and observation.

claim: Out of 12 cells that responded to capsaicin and showed a rise in global fluorescence due to Ca2+ influx, nine cells had easily distinguished local micro-domains of Ca2+ influx that we classified as sparklets.
source: Out of 12 cells that responded to capsaicin and showed a rise in global fluorescence due to Ca2+ influx, nine cells had easily distinguished local micro-domains of Ca2+ influx that we classified as sparklets.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: Fluorescence intensity analysis of TRPV1 sparklets in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons revealed two states: a dark state presumed to correspond to a closed channel state and a bright state presumed to correspond an open channel state.
source: Fluorescence intensity analysis of TRPV1 sparklets in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons revealed two states: a dark state presumed to correspond to a closed channel state and a bright state presumed to correspond an open channel state (Figure 1A and Video 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: Sparklet-to-sparklet variability in amplitude of the capsaicin-induced fluorescence was low.
source: All-points amplitude histograms of the fluorescence intensity revealed that sparklet-to-sparklet variability in amplitude of the capsaicin-induced fluorescence was low (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The two-state intensity traces resemble those of single-channel activity measured with electrophysiology.
source: Interestingly, the two-state intensity traces (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1) resemble those of single-channel activity measured with electrophysiology (e.g., Liu et al., 2004; Rosenbaum et al., 2004), albeit with lower temporal resolution.
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature supported by citations.

claim: The data are consistent with each sparklet representing a single gating TRPV1 channel or a cluster of TRPV1 channels gating cooperatively.
source: These data are consistent with each sparklet representing a single gating TRPV1 channel or a cluster of TRPV1 channels gating cooperatively.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: The current recorded in the presence of 100 nM capsaicin normalized to the current at a saturating capsaicin concentration was 0.84 ± 0.05 (n = 4).
source: Examining the dose–response relation for activation by capsaicin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) shows that the current recorded in the presence of 100 nM capsaicin normalized to the current at a saturating capsaicin concentration was 0.84 ± 0.05 (n = 4).
evidence: This is an experimental measurement shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The mean open probability of sparklets was 0.7 ± 0.1 (N = 5).
source: This fractional activation value is slightly greater than the open probability values plotted in Figure 1D, for which the mean was 0.7 ± 0.1 (N = 5).
evidence: This is an experimental measurement shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The sensitivity of single TRPV1 channels as calculated from optical recordings of sparklets is similar to that of the cell population measured using whole-cell patch clamp.
source: These data indicate that the sensitivity of single TRPV1 channels as calculated from optical recordings of sparklets is similar to that of the cell population measured using whole-cell patch clamp.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing sparklet data to whole-cell patch clamp data.

claim: Many of the capsaicin-activated sparklets observed were dynamic, that is they appeared to move laterally in the plane of the membrane.
source: However, many of the capsaicin-activated sparklets we observed were dynamic, that is they appeared to move laterally in the plane of the membrane (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Simultaneous mobility in the plasma membrane and gating has not been previously reported for any ion channel.
source: To our knowledge, simultaneous mobility in the plasma membrane and gating has not been previously reported for any ion channel, and are explored further below.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding based on knowledge of the literature.

claim: The heterogeneity of TRPV1 mobilities, with some sparklets immobile and others dynamic, indicates that the population of TRPV1 channels was heterogeneous in some aspect of channel structure or function.
source: The heterogeneity of TRPV1 mobilities, with some sparklets immobile and others dynamic, indicates that the population of TRPV1 channels was heterogeneous in some aspect of channel structure or function.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed heterogeneity in mobility.

claim: The appearance of individual sparklets when capsaicin was added became difficult to discern over time as the fluorescence across the cell footprint increased.
source: The appearance of individual sparklets when capsaicin was added became difficult to discern over time as the fluorescence across the cell footprint increased.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: The increase in fluorescence 'background' was due to the rapid, global increase in intracellular Ca2+ that occurs over the course of our experiments.
source: The increase in fluorescence 'background' was due to the rapid, global increase in intracellular Ca2+ that occurs over the course of our experiments.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observation.

claim: The Ca2+ chelator EGTA (10 mM) in the intracellular solution extended the useful recording time by acting as a Ca2+ sink.
source: Although the Ca2+ chelator EGTA (10 mM) in our intracellular solution extended the useful recording time by acting as a Ca2+ sink, a rise in global Ca2+ due to continued influx of Ca2+ through TRPV1 ultimately obscured the sparklet signals once intracellular Ca2+ levels exceeded the upper limit of the Ca2+ sensitive dye's optimal range (Fluo-4: 1 μM Ca2+; Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental design and observations.

claim: Tube-like structures prevalent within the footprint of isolated neurons brightened markedly when capsaicin was added.
source: The second factor limiting our interpretation of sparklet activity in dorsal root ganglion neurons are the tube-like structures prevalent within the footprint of isolated neurons that brightened markedly when capsaicin was added.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: The tube-like structures are likely neurite-like processes underneath the cell footprint, rather than endoplasmic reticulum within the cell body.
source: These tube-like structures were observed even when the SERCA inhibitor thapsigargin was present (Video 3), indicating that they are likely neurite-like processes underneath the cell footprint, rather than endoplasmic reticulum within the cell body.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that the structures persist in the presence of thapsigargin.

claim: TRPV1-tagRFP and TRPV1-GFP in HEK293T/17 cells showed mobile and immobile capsaicin-activated sparklets.
source: We found that, like isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons, TRPV1-tagRFP and TRPV1-GFP in HEK293T/17 cells showed mobile and immobile capsaicin-activated sparklets (Video 6).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Video 6.

claim: Sparklets were not observed in the absence of capsaicin nor in the absence of extracellular Ca2+.
source: Sparklets were not observed in the absence of capsaicin nor in the absence of extracellular Ca2+ (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fluorescence from capsaicin-activated sparklets in HEK293T/17 cells had the signature two-amplitude intensities also observed in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons.
source: As shown in Figure 2B,C (see also Video 7), fluorescence from capsaicin-activated sparklets in HEK293T/17 cells had the signature two-amplitude intensities also observed in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figures 2B,C and Video 7.

claim: The amplitude of fluorescence intensity in the sparklets was comparable in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons and HEK293T/17 cells.
source: Interestingly, the amplitude of fluorescence intensity in the sparklets was comparable in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons and HEK293T/17 cells (compare Figure 2D to Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 2D.

claim: The open probability for sparklets in HEK293T/17 cells was significantly less than for sparklets in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons.
source: The open probability for sparklets in HEK293T/17 cells was significantly less than for sparklets in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The difference in open probability is consistent with the higher K1/2 for activation of TRPV1 expressed in HEK293T/17 cells.
source: This difference is consistent with the higher K1/2 for activation of TRPV1 expressed in HEK293T/17 cells (Collins and Gordon, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Capsaicin-independent increases in local Ca2+ were observed in untransfected as well as TRPV1-transfected HEK293T/17 cells.
source: Interestingly, capsaicin-independent increases in local Ca2+ were observed in untransfected as well as TRPV1-transfected HEK293T/17 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: Capsaicin-independent Ca2+ events could be easily distinguished from sparklets due to TRPV1 as their open times were very brief and their amplitude was spikey.
source: These could be easily distinguished from sparklets due to TRPV1 as their open times were very brief and their amplitude was spikey (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), rather than showing two states like TRPV1 (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figures 2B,C.

claim: Each fluorescent spot represents one and only one TRPV1 channel.
source: Each fluorescent spot represents one and only one TRPV1 channel
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by photobleaching experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: TRPV1 is a homomeric tetramer structurally similar to the voltage-gated superfamily of ion channels that includes voltage-gated K+ channels.
source: TRPV1 is a homomeric tetramer structurally similar to the voltage-gated superfamily of ion channels that includes voltage-gated K+ channels (Liao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Each TRPV1-GFP channel should have four copies of GFP per functional channel.
source: Each TRPV1-GFP channel should thus have four copies of GFP per functional channel.
evidence: This is an inference from the tetrameric structure of TRPV1.

claim: Using a high-intensity laser to image the fluorescence from individual TRPV1-GFP features produced sudden decreases in fluorescence intensity, each of which is presumed to represent photobleaching of a single GFP.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, using a high-intensity laser to image the fluorescence from individual TRPV1-GFP features produced sudden decreases in fluorescence intensity, each of which is presumed to represent photobleaching of a single GFP (Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 3A, supported by a citation.

claim: The best fit for the photobleaching data was obtained using n = 4 and p = 0.45.
source: The best fit was obtained using n = 4 and p = 0.45 (Figure 3B), and fits with n = 5, as would be the case if TRPV1 were pentameric, or n = 8, if TRPV1 tetrameric channels formed pairs, were both rejected by χ2 goodness-of-fit tests (Figure 3C and legend).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Fits with n = 5 or n = 8 were rejected by χ2 goodness-of-fit tests.
source: The best fit was obtained using n = 4 and p = 0.45 (Figure 3B), and fits with n = 5, as would be the case if TRPV1 were pentameric, or n = 8, if TRPV1 tetrameric channels formed pairs, were both rejected by χ2 goodness-of-fit tests (Figure 3C and legend).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Together with the two-state fluorescence intensity of capsaicin-induced sparklets, the photobleaching data indicate that each TRPV1-GFP feature represented one channel, with four subunits, rather than two or more channels, with eight or more subunits.
source: Together with the two-state fluorescence intensity of capsaicin-induced sparklets, these data indicate that each TRPV1-GFP feature represented one channel, with four subunits, rather than two or more channels, with eight or more subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the photobleaching and sparklet data.

claim: The large variability in channel mobilities, with a 20-fold range of Deff (0.01–0.5 μm2/s), is consistent with a heterogeneous population within any given cell.
source: The large variability in channel mobilities, with a 20-fold range of Deff (0.01–0.5 μm2/s), is consistent with a heterogeneous population within any given cell.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The distribution of mobilities between cells varied by about a factor of two (mean Deff range: 0.029 to 0.056 μm2/s).
source: Interestingly, the distribution of mobilities between cells also varied, but only by about a factor of two (mean Deff range: 0.029 to 0.056 μm2/s) (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The co-localization between TRPV1-GFP and the Ca2+ sparklets confirmed that mobile sparklets co-diffuse with mobile TRPV1-GFP channels.
source: First, the co-localization between TRPV1-GFP (Figure 5C, red circles) and the Ca2+ sparklets (Figure 5C, cyan circles) confirmed that mobile sparklets co-diffuse with mobile TRPV1-GFP channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The higher fluorescence intensity of sparklets compared to TRPV1-GFP did not impede the ability to localize sparklets as compared to TRPV1-GFP.
source: Second, the higher fluorescence intensity of sparklets compared to TRPV1-GFP did not impede our ability to localize sparklets as compared to TRPV1-GFP.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The simplest interpretation of the data is that sparklets represent Ca2+ flux through the labeled TRPV1-GFP as it gates.
source: The simplest interpretation of our data is that sparklets represent Ca2+ flux through the labeled TRPV1-GFP as it gates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The mobility of actively gating TRPV1 is somewhat surprising, as Ca2+ sparklets from TRPV4 were previously reported to be immobile.
source: The mobility of actively gating TRPV1 is somewhat surprising, as Ca2+ sparklets from TRPV4 were previously reported to be immobile (Mercado et al., 2014) as have sparklets attributed to L-type Ca2+ channels (Navedo et al., 2005; Navedo et al., 2006) and AchR channels (Demuro and Parker, 2005).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature supported by citations.

claim: In a search of the literature, no reports of simultaneous observations of ion channel activity and mobility in living cells were found.
source: In addition, in a search of the literature we did not find any reports of simultaneous observations of ion channel activity and mobility in living cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding based on knowledge of the literature.

claim: The mobility of capsaicin-activated TRPV1 sparklets in three different cell types raises the question of whether the mobility of other types of active channels should be reexamined.
source: However, the mobility of capsaicin-activated TRPV1 sparklets in three different cell types (isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons, F11 cells, and HEK293T/17 cells) raises the question of whether the mobility of other types of active channels should be reexamined.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Capsaicin appeared to decrease the mobility of TRPV1-GFP channels.
source: Upon examining a large number of mobile TRPV1-GFP channels under various conditions, we noticed that capsaicin appeared to decrease their mobility.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: Channel mobility might be regulated as a function of channel activity.
source: We therefore hypothesized that channel mobility might be regulated as a function of channel activity.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations.

claim: In control experiments with nominally Ca2+-free extracellular buffer and in which the cells were not subject to voltage clamp, a trend of increasing MSD was observed.
source: In control experiments with nominally Ca2+-free extracellular buffer and in which the cells were not subject to voltage clamp, we observed a trend of increasing MSD (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The observation-induced increase in apparent mobility was speculated to be due to photodamage by the excitation light.
source: Although we did not study this effect further, we speculate it was due to photodamage by the excitation light.
evidence: This is a speculation about the cause of the observed effect.

claim: In cells treated with 1 μM capsaicin and remaining in a Ca2+-containing solution, the RΔMSD of TRPV1-GFP in a given cell decreased upon the addition of capsaicin.
source: In cells treated with 1 μM capsaicin and remaining in a Ca2+-containing solution (but, as in control experiments, not voltage clamped), the RΔMSD of TRPV1-GFP in a given cell decreased upon the addition of capsaicin, indicating that the TRPV1 channels exhibited a decrease in mobility as they opened in the presence of Ca2+ (Figure 6B, blue).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In control experiments that switched from a Ca2+-containing solution to a nominally Ca2+-free solution without capsaicin or to a nominally Ca2+-free solution with capsaicin, no significant change between RΔMSD in before and after videos was observed.
source: In control experiments that switched from a Ca2+-containing solution to a nominally Ca2+-free solution without capsaicin (Figure 6B, green) or to a nominally Ca2+-free solution with capsaicin (Figure 6B, red) no significant change between RΔMSD in our before and after videos was observed.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The decrease in mobility required both channel activation (i.e., capsaicin) and Ca2+ influx.
source: Thus, the decrease in RΔMSD required both channel activation (i.e., capsaicin) and Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The mobility of TRPV1-GFP decreased in a capsaicin- and Ca2+-dependent manner.
source: Our data indicate that the mobility of TRPV1-GFP decreased in a capsaicin- and Ca2+-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: 13 out of 16 sparklets analyzed during a period when they remained open and observable showed a capsaicin-dependent decrease in mobility.
source: We found that 13 out of 16 sparklets analyzed during a period when they remained open and observable showed a capsaicin-dependent decrease in mobility (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 7.

claim: Activation of TRPV1 yielded a decrease in channel mobility, whether observed as the GFP-fusion protein or as sparklets.
source: In conclusion, activation of TRPV1 yielded a decrease in channel mobility, whether observed as the GFP-fusion protein or as sparklets.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: TRPV1 sparklets are a new tool to address critical gaps in knowledge concerning the function of TRPV1 in its native plasma membrane environment.
source: TRPV1 sparklets are a new tool to address critical gaps in our knowledge concerning the function of TRPV1 in its native plasma membrane environment and opens the door to further exploration into how plasma membrane dynamics and cell signaling regulate TRPV1 function.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: Synchronous recording of localization and activity of native TRPV1 channels in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons and of TRPV1-GFP or TRPV1-tagRFP channels in transiently-transfected HEK293T/17 cells revealed a surprising range of mobilities in the plasma membrane.
source: Synchronous recording of localization and activity of native TRPV1 channels in isolated dorsal root ganglion neurons and of TRPV1-GFP or TRPV1-tagRFP channels in transiently-transfected HEK293T/17 cells revealed a surprising range of mobilities in the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Some sparklets diffused at a rate comparable to that expected for an individual lipid (∼1 µm2/s).
source: Like the L-type Ca2+ channels (Navedo et al., 2005; Navedo et al., 2006), AchR channels (Demuro and Parker, 2005), and TRPV4 channels (Mercado et al., 2014) discussed above, some sparklets were immobile, whereas others diffused at a rate comparable to that expected for an individual lipid (∼1 µm2/s) (Golebiewska et al., 2008) (Figures 1, 2, 5 and 7).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by a citation for the expected lipid diffusion rate.

claim: Gating of channels as they diffuse in the plasma membrane has not been previously reported, although synchronous gating and diffusion may well represent the 'natural' behavior of many channels and transporters.
source: To our knowledge, gating of channels as they diffuse in the plasma membrane has not been previously reported, although synchronous gating and diffusion may well represent the 'natural' behavior of many channels and transporters.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding and speculation about its generality.

claim: Sparklets have been used previously by Navedo et al. to report on the gating of L-type Ca2+ channels as single channels or in clusters of up to seven channels.
source: Sparklets have been used previously by Navedo et al. to report on the gating of L-type Ca2+ channels as single channels or in clusters of up to seven channels (Navedo et al., 2005), or assemblies of TRPV4 channels in arterial myocytes (Mercado et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The two-state fluorescence signature of the TRPV1-tagRFP sparklets could arise from single-channel openings or from multiple channels at each sparklet site with very high gating cooperativity.
source: The two-state fluorescence signature of the TRPV1-tagRFP sparklets could arise from single-channel openings or from multiple channels at each sparklet site with very high gating cooperativity (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Analysis of the photobleaching steps attributed to TRPV1-GFP channels in fixed HEK293T/17 cells provided further confirmation that the channel assembles as a tetramer of TRPV1-GFP subunits without forming higher order oligomeric assemblies.
source: Analysis of the photobleaching steps attributed to TRPV1-GFP channels in fixed HEK293T/17 cells provided further confirmation that the channel assembles as a tetramer of TRPV1-GFP subunits without forming higher order oligomeric assemblies (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Laterally mobile TRPV1-GFP in live cells could be tracked via both their fluorescent protein label and their sparklet activity.
source: Importantly, laterally mobile TRPV1-GFP in live cells could be tracked via both their fluorescent protein label and their sparklet activity, and switching from a lower fluorescence emission of the fluorescent protein label to the higher intensity sparklet fluorescence within the same feature demonstrated that the mobile sparklets emanated from mobile TRPV1-GFP (Figure 5 and Video 9 and Video 10).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5 and Videos 9 and 10.

claim: Each capsaicin-induced sparklet is due to the activation of one, and only one, TRPV1 ion channel.
source: Together, these data indicate that each capsaicin-induced sparklet is due to the activation of one, and only one, TRPV1 ion channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the photobleaching and sparklet data.

claim: The data on dorsal root ganglion sparklets activated by capsaicin recapitulates observations in TRPV1-GFP and TRPV1-tagRFP expressing HEK293T/17 cells.
source: Our data on dorsal root ganglion sparklets activated by capsaicin recapitulates our observations in TRPV1-GFP and TRPV1-tagRFP expressing HEK293T/17 cells (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data across cell types.

claim: The finding that Ca2+ influx is required for the capsaicin-induced decrease in TRPV1 mobility may hint at the mechanism by which the change in mobility occurs.
source: However, our finding that Ca2+ influx is required for the capsaicin-induced decrease in TRPV1 mobility may hint at the mechanism by which the change in mobility occurs.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claim: Changes in the cytoskeleton upon upregulation of Ca2+-sensitive effectors such as α-actinin, gelsolin or scinderin can be easily imagined to regulate membrane protein mobility.
source: Changes in the cytoskeleton upon upregulation of Ca2+-sensitive effectors such as α-actinin, gelsolin or scinderin (Rodriguez Del Castillo et al., 1990; Witke et al., 1993; Kinosian et al., 1998) can be easily imagined to regulate membrane protein mobility.
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to prior literature on Ca2+-sensitive cytoskeletal proteins.

claim: The formation of local Ca2+ domains has previously been linked to regulation of cell architecture and remodeling of the cytoskeleton.
source: The formation of local Ca2+ domains has previously been linked to regulation of cell architecture and remodeling of the cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: A recent study looking at the influence of TRPM7 elicited Ca2+ micro-domains in migrating fibroblasts identified this process as part of the mechanism by which the cell steers towards a chemoattractant.
source: A recent study looking at the influence of TRPM7 elicited Ca2+ micro-domains in migrating fibroblasts identified this process as part of the mechanism by which the cell steers towards a chemoattractant (Wei et al., 2009, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The involvement of cytoskeleton in the Ca2+-influx mediated regulation of TRPV1 mobility is a subject of interest for future studies.
source: Thus, the involvement of cytoskeleton in the Ca2+-influx mediated regulation of TRPV1 mobility is a subject of interest for future studies.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: TRPV1 binds to several proteins important to cell signaling, including the p85β subunit of PI3-kinase and the TrkA receptor.
source: We and others have shown that TRPV1 binds to several proteins important to cell signaling, including the p85β subunit of PI3-kinase and the TrkA receptor (Chuang et al., 2001; Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: These interactions are likely related to a physiological response facilitated by nerve growth factor (NGF) that increases cell surface expression of TRPV1.
source: These interactions are likely related to a physiological response facilitated by nerve growth factor (NGF) that increases cell surface expression of TRPV1 (Zhang et al., 2005; Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Biochemical and electrophysiological experiments point to a complex formed between AKAP79/150 and TRPV1 to alter sensitization of TRPV1 in response to inflammatory agents.
source: Biochemical and electrophysiological experiments also point to a complex formed between AKAP79/150 and TRPV1 to alter sensitization of TRPV1 in response to inflammatory agents (Zhang et al., 2008; Por et al., 2010; Efendiev et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Differential properties of a signaling complex involving TRPV1 could be determined by the mobility of the channel, which makes its activity dependent mobility a point of interest.
source: Differential properties of a signaling complex involving TRPV1 could be determined by the mobility of the channel, which makes its activity dependent mobility a point of interest.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of the findings.

claim: The activity of TRPV1 may confine the channel to a specific region of the cell, where it may (or may not) be more likely to encounter its binding partners in the PI3-kinase/TrkA receptor complex.
source: One can imagine that the activity of TRPV1 will confine the channel to a specific region of the cell, where it may (or may not) be more likely to encounter its binding partners in the PI3-kinase/ TrkA receptor complex.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of the findings.

claim: It is possible that the binding of TRPV1 to a complex with a consequent change to the channel's mobility also feeds back on its function.
source: It is further possible that the binding of TRPV1 to a complex with a consequent change to the channel's mobility also feeds back on its function.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential regulatory mechanisms.

claim: Decreased mobility in regions of locally elevated channel activity may serve as a sort of diffusion trap, concentrating TRPV1 channels in parts of the cell where they are most needed.
source: Perhaps decreased mobility in regions of locally elevated channel activity serves as a sort of diffusion trap, concentrating TRPV1 channels in parts of the cell where they are most needed.
evidence: This is a speculation about the physiological role of the findings.

claim: Sensory neurons with cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia are not very polarized.
source: Sensory neurons with cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia are not very polarized (Dubin and Patapoutian, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In culture without other types of neurons, sensory neurons do not form synapses; in their role as sensory receptors they are not postsynaptic to other cells types and appear to have lost the signaling required to form postsynaptic structures.
source: Indeed, in culture without other types of neurons they do not form synapses; in their role as sensory receptors they are not postsynaptic to other cells types and appear to have lost the signaling required to form postsynaptic structures.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about sensory neurons.

claim: Other mechanisms for protein targeting might be prominent in sensory neurons.
source: Other mechanisms for protein targeting might thus be prominent in these types of cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the properties of sensory neurons.
